justifications.clinical.efficiency: ABPTS ECS exam; experience requirements; niche and significant investment.
justifications.clinical.caseloadApplicability: Very narrow applicability; EMG and NCS services restricted to specific scope in most states.
justifications.clinical.reimbursement: EMG and NCS have CPT codes; PT billing for these is restricted in most states; scope issues limit billing value.
justifications.clinical.marketDemand: Very limited employer demand; one of the least-held ABPTS certifications.
justifications.business.cashPayViability: EMG/NCS and wound electrotherapy are hospital/physician-referred — almost no cash-pay pathway.
justifications.business.pricingLeverage: Hospital contracts may pay well, but private-practice pricing power is minimal.
justifications.business.marketDifferentiation: Extremely rare credential (smallest ABPTS specialty), so highly differentiated — but in a narrow market.
justifications.business.ownerLeverage: Hard to scale; services tied tightly to the credentialed clinician and medical referral chain.
justifications.business.marketDemand: Negligible consumer recognition; referrals are physician-driven.
justifications.business.efficiency: Steep prerequisites, exam difficulty, and limited residency pathways make this very costly.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyRecognition: ABPTS board cert — strong faculty credential, especially for modalities/neuro-rehab content.
justifications.academicClinical.scholarship: Smaller research community than OCS/NCS but recognized within rehab science.
justifications.academicClinical.teachingValue: Anchors EMG/NCS, modalities, and integumentary content in DPT curricula.
justifications.academicClinical.evidenceDepth: Reasonable evidence for diagnostic EMG; e-stim/wound evidence is mixed.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyDemand: Rarely listed in postings; programs cover this content with generalists.
